# OpenAdapt Blog

> Technical posts, benchmarks, and automation recipes from the OpenAdapt project — an open-source governed compiler for repeated GUI work. Record a workflow once, compile it, replay it deterministically; under UI drift it re-resolves from retained evidence or halts.

## Posts
- [The silent wrong write: your automation should halt instead of guessing](https://blog.openadapt.ai/posts/silent-wrong-action/): Screen-only verification silently passed 5 of 7 transactional fault classes. Measured end to end through the real replayer over 90 runs per arm, a screen-only oracle silently accepted 75.0% of the wrong effects that actually occurred (54/90 runs); adding one out-of-band oracle that reads the system of record cut that to 12.5% (9/90), and a complete read path over every mutable surface reaches 0/90. All nine residual misses are one class: a collateral write to a surface the oracle does not read.
- [We ran it on a real EMR. The compiler won.](https://blog.openadapt.ai/posts/openemr-benchmark/): Compiled workflows vs. a frontier computer-use agent on real OpenEMR — 20/20 vs. 10/10 task success, 1.8x faster, $0 vs. $0.55 per run; with agent fallback, $0.029 vs. $0.238 per successful run.
- [The 500th run: compiled automation vs. computer-use agents](https://blog.openadapt.ai/posts/the-500th-run/): Same task, same success check — 100/100 for the compiled script vs. 20/20 for the agent, at 4.9 s vs. 37.5 s and $0 vs. $0.27 per run.
